scope: The spec map requirement-by-repo coverage matrix. Belongs here: the matrix rows; the src, test, src+test, and dash rendering; the webapp matrix view. Does not belong here: full-text retrieval (QURY). Boundary case: MAP stays its own domain because the webapp matrix view will accrue here.

requirements.statement: spec map renders the cross-repo requirement-to-repo coverage matrix derived from tags, with per-cell src/test/src+test states.
requirements.why: The platform coverage view a single-repo scan cannot give.

requirements.statement: When spec map is run, the spec CLI shall render the requirement-by-member-repo coverage matrix derived from @spec tags, marking each cell as src, test, src+test, or uncovered.
requirements.why: Without the cross-repo matrix, a requirement covered in one member and silently absent in another looks done — no single-repo scan can show which member lags.

requirements.statement: When spec get is run with a requirement id, the spec CLI shall print that requirement's full record from the derived index, or print [] on stdout with guidance on stderr and exit 0 when the id is unknown.
requirements.why: An agent that needs a requirement's statement, status, and version today has to start spec serve or grep SPEC.json; every other read has a CLI verb.

requirements.statement: When spec list is run, the spec CLI shall print every requirement record in (key, seq) order, filtered to one domain by --domain and to one status by --status when given.
requirements.why: spec query excludes superseded and deprecated rows and ranks by relevance, so nothing enumerates the catalog as records, in order, including history.

requirements.statement: When spec get prints a requirement, the spec CLI shall list its implementing sites and its verifying sites, each a file and line read from the code tags, sorted by repo, file, and line.
requirements.why: The code tags are the only record of where a requirement is built and proved, so a reader who cannot see them from the requirement goes back to grepping the tree.

requirements.statement: When spec get runs with a requirement id, it shall print that requirement's full record.
requirements.why: An agent that needs a requirement's statement, status, and version today has to start spec serve or grep SPEC.json; every other read has a CLI verb.

requirements.statement: When spec get is given an unknown requirement id, it shall print [] and exit 0.
requirements.why: If an unknown id failed the command, an agent probing for an id would treat a normal empty answer as an error.
